old_str:
Probashi Kallyan desk [D0185, GD0051].
- Bangladeshi workers found HIV-positive in Middle Eastern countries are sent home in haste without any treatment, a practice of many years, a Prothom Alo editorial said in February 2026; WHO (the World Health Organization) and the ILO (International Labour Organization) have said expelling someone only for HIV is discriminatory [GD0028, GD0032]. The editorial said that at home medicine is free but counselling, mental-health support and livelihood help are very limited, that many are afraid to tell even their families, and that although an HIV-negative certificate is mandatory before going abroad, workers get no practical training on risk or sexual health [GD0029, GD0030, GD0031]. Later economic help follows counselling and training under the EU-BRAC Prottasha-2 project [D0187]. The EU delegation's programme manager said in August 2026 that EU-funded reintegration work began in 2017 and that the projects run through BRAC and IOM are essentially a pilot [AB0140].
